Donald Trump has been active on Truth Social, sharing his thoughts and feelings on a number of matters (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump has launched a blistering online tirade against NATO "freeloaders," using an extraordinary social media outburst to name and shame European allies.

Writing on Truth Social ahead of a major summit, the president laid bare a stark financial breakdown to blast what he views as a deeply unfair alliance. "The United States spends more money on NATO than any other country, by far, to protect them, without getting any benefit from so doing," Trump roared in the explosive post.

He then listed his own eye-watering spending figures spanning from 2014 to 2025, claiming the U.S. has shelled out a staggering $999 billion.

By contrast, he called out the United Kingdom at $90.5 billion, France at $66.5 billion, Italy at $48.8 billion, and Poland at $44.3 billion.

Slamming the rest of the alliance, Trump added: "Others, including Germany, are MUCH LOWER. (2014-2025) Ridiculous! President DJT."

He went on a rant, attacking five NATO countries, who he believes are being given unfair treatment

While the numbers sent shockwaves through social media, defense experts were quick to punch holes in the president's math.

The eye-watering $999 billion figure appears to conflate the total annual U.S. domestic defense budget with direct alliance contributions. In reality, the actual annual collective NATO budget sits at roughly $6 billion.

Furthermore, NATO does not operate on a subscription or membership fee basis.

Instead, it relies on individual nations meeting voluntary defense spending targets relative to their own GDP, in other words, European allies do not technically owe the U.S. money.

Despite the disputed math, the furious outburst exposes a deep and bitter rift currently brewing inside the administration.

Washington has grown increasingly angry with European partners over their outright refusal to assist with recent U.S. military operations in Iran and the highly volatile Strait of Hormuz.

While Trump claims allies are failing to pay their fair share, official data shows European defense expenditures have actually skyrocketed in recent years under heavy pressure from Washington.

The explosive remarks ensure a fiercely combative atmosphere at the upcoming NATO summit in Ankara, where military burden-sharing is set to spark an almighty showdown.
